facts.detail: White means no gigabit infrastructure exists and none is likely within three years.
Grey means one qualifying gigabit infrastructure is available or planned within three years.
Black means two or more qualifying gigabit infrastructures from different suppliers are available or planned.
Under Review covers unverified current claims or planned delivery with risks or evidence gaps.
BDUK only provides subsidy to target premises designated White; Under Review may enter deferred scope pending further review.

guard_streams.write_limit: Official OMR, programme, methodology, checker, planned-build or aggregate evidence cannot establish current fixed-broadband availability, live orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel; exact corrected Ofcom r2 postcode-row matching remains mandatory.

facts.detail: The January 2026 OMR classified 2,990,617 England and Wales premises as White.
It classified 2,179,083 premises as Under Review.
It classified 9,157,988 premises as Grey.
It classified 16,726,869 premises as Black.
The four classifications totalled 31,054,557 premises.

facts.detail: A previous National Rolling OMR submission may be reused when no update is received, but reuse is not guaranteed.
Suppliers are encouraged to keep coverage data and evidence current, ideally no more than six months old.
Although data was collected UK-wide, the January 2026 assessed outcome was limited to England and Wales.
The supplied UPRN lists were sourced from AddressBase Premium Epoch 123.
Ordnance Survey published that AddressBase epoch on 27 November 2025.

facts.detail: The RFI baseline retains postal-address classifications D, C or L and excludes N non-postal values.
The baseline accepts country codes E, W, S or N.
BLPU StateCode 4 demolished premises are excluded.
LogicalStatusCode must be 1 approved or 6 provisional.
When duplicate UPRNs are removed, approved records take priority over provisional records.

facts.detail: The BDUK gigabit address checker is for addresses in England and Wales.
The service reports whether gigabit broadband is available or planned for an address.
The checker currently uses January OMR data published in June 2026.
BDUK says the checker data will next be updated in September 2026.
BDUK cannot guarantee complete address-status accuracy because supplier plans and external-source processing can change.
